title: RAG: Embeddings, Chunking & Vector Search with ChromaDB
why: LLMs only know their training cutoff data and cannot see your proprietary documents. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) connects your agent to external documents and internal databases with real-time vector search.
objectives: Understand high-dimensional text embeddings and cosine similarity
Implement document chunking strategies (recursive character splitting)
Index and query documents using ChromaDB
concept: Chunking splits large documents into semantic pieces (e.g. 500 characters with 50 character overlap). An embedding model maps each chunk to a dense float vector. When a user asks a query, nearest neighbors are retrieved and injected into the prompt.

code.content:
import math

def cosine_similarity(vec_a: list[float], vec_b: list[float]) -> float:
    dot_product = sum(a * b for a, b in zip(vec_a, vec_b))
    norm_a = math.sqrt(sum(a * a for a in vec_a))
    norm_b = math.sqrt(sum(b * b for b in vec_b))
    return dot_product / (norm_a * norm_b) if norm_a and norm_b else 0.0

# Mock 3-dimensional embeddings
q_vec = [0.8, 0.2, 0.5]
doc1_vec = [0.75, 0.25, 0.45]  # Highly similar
doc2_vec = [-0.1, 0.9, -0.3]  # Low similarity

print(f'Similarity to Doc 1: {cosine_similarity(q_vec, doc1_vec):.4f}')
print(f'Similarity to Doc 2: {cosine_similarity(q_vec, doc2_vec):.4f}')

practice.description: Write a recursive chunking function that splits text into chunks of at most 200 characters preserving whole words.
practice.hint: Split by spaces and accumulate words until the length exceeds 200.

requirements: Load text from documents, chunk into 500-char segments
Query nearest chunks and pass as context into an LLM synthesis prompt

checklist: Understood vector spaces and cosine similarity
Implemented text chunking with overlap to preserve context
Integrated retrieved passages into an LLM answer prompt
mistakes: Chunking too large (exceeding token window) or too small (losing semantic meaning)
